Two years ago, Sonos expanded from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphones category. Reports indicate that Sonos is preparing a more premium successor product that incorporates artificial intelligence.

Sonos Ace Ultra Headphones Are Set to Debut

Chris Welch reported for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra as a premium successor to its 2024 Ace headphones.

A U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) filing discovered on Monday mentions the product and indicates that there may be up to five color options, an increase from the black and white choices offered with the original model.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September, and the timing of the current filing suggests the Ace Ultra may be unveiled at that event.

The filing also contains technical clues indicating that the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged that the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration features upon launch and failed to stand out in a competitive market.

This time, Sonos appears to be planning to tie its hardware more directly to its broader AI strategy.

Conrad described the company's growth opportunities as conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home environment, noting that Sonos devices can serve as hardware that operates across rooms and understands household living patterns.

The company has expanded its Sonos voice control functionality to include operation of Philips Hue and Lutron Caséta devices.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March, equipped with the H2 chip, enhanced noise cancellation, and live translation. Siri AI will also extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For more information about the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, please refer to the full Bloomberg report.
